title: When the Thunder Speaks
identity: Frederick Fox's *When the Thunder Speaks* (1998) is an approximately 13-minute, one-movement work for alto saxophone and piano, commissioned by Thomas Liley and published by Dorn. A University of North Texas dissertation analyzes the work and reports extended saxophone and piano techniques; its author found no recording at the time of writing.

evidence.claim: UNT dissertation gives alto saxophone and piano, approximate duration 13 minutes, a Thomas Liley commission, one-movement sectional structure organized primarily by tempo, no known recordings, and work-specific technique information: timbral trill (mm. 32-34), growling (mm. 32-34), pitch bending (m. 145), slap tonguing (m. 249); the piano uses fingertip glissandos, palms on strings, and muted keys. Pages 69-70 explain the saxophone effects and the source says the piece uses standard notation.
evidence.source_name: University of North Texas doctoral dissertation

evidence.claim: Indiana University Jacobs School of Music lists *When the Thunder Speaks* (1998) among Fox’s solo works and gives publisher listings including Dorn.
evidence.source_name: Indiana University Jacobs School of Music composer page

review_focus: The dissertation identifies timbral trill, growling, pitch bending, and slap tonguing in the saxophone part, alongside fingertip glissandos, palms on strings, and muted keys in the piano. These documented effects offer concrete score-review points; the dissertation reports standard notation and no non-conventional rhythmic notation.
collection_flag: Commissioned by saxophonist Thomas Liley. The UNT author reports no known recording at the time of the dissertation and describes this as Fox's final composition.

score_links.description: Public doctoral dissertation includes analytical discussion of the work; score plates/analysis pages should be consulted.

gaps: The dissertation excerpts include publisher-permission score examples, but no full saxophone score was inspected; exact written range remains unknown.
Recording status may have changed since the dissertation; no recording was located in this pass.
